analysis.title: AI Derisk: what we are seeing (Ellinikaki) / Prime Perspective: AI Unwinds
key_insights: Equities had two very difficult sessions with a severe derisking across the AI complex. GS Prime, Trading and Execution views frame the drivers, flows and performance.

The desk's bottom line: credit is forcing a rethink of how quickly the AI capex cycle can be financed and delivered, and the positioning unwind amplified the move. With AI exposure materially reduced, discretionary nets low and rates rallying, trading sees pockets of overreaction, while financing constraints remain real.

Triggers cited: whether credit markets can keep financing the AI buildout, acute pressure in neoclouds and hyperscaler credit, OpenAI revenue concerns, China memory breakthroughs, datacenter sentiment into the midterms, power/supply constraints and further issuance. Hotter CPI added near-term hike risk.

Flows were predominantly risk-off from hedge funds, with selling concentrated in AI. Long-only funds bought defensives and quality and sold financials. Global equities were net sold on Oct 14 at -2.1 SDs vs 1-year, with long sales outpacing short sales about 3:1.

Global AI stocks saw the second-largest net selling in the past year (-2.8 Z score). Hedge funds net sold the basket for five consecutive sessions (Oct 8-14), reversing all cumulative HF net buying since the start of 2025.

AI net allocation fell to 26.1% from 31.7% at the early-June peak. The AI long/short ratio fell to 3.27 from 4.34, the 7th percentile vs the past year. Overall HF net leverage is down 4.3 pts MTD to 73.3%, the 6th percentile vs the past year.

Trading view (Rich Privo): demand for compute can grow exponentially but the capital to finance it cannot. Credit widening across the AI vertical is a warning, and the equilibrium may require recalibrating what can be delivered and when. This favours firms with powered capacity and strong balance sheets over leveraged middlemen.

Privo argues the structural AI thesis can stay intact even if the investment cycle disappoints, and that much bad news is now priced. Neoclouds are down 20% in five sessions, which he calls a historic liquidation. Quality has rallied in 16 of 18 sessions with RSI at 83. His gut is that the market overreacted in pockets.

Hedge fund performance through Oct 14 close: TMT L/S -2.7% on the day and -4.5% MTD. Global Fundamental L/S -0.9% on the day and -2.1% MTD. Asia-focused L/S -0.9% and -4.1% MTD. Systematic funds were the relative winner at +0.5% on the day and +1.9% MTD.

US equities were 66% of global net selling on Oct 14 (-1.8 SDs), with long and short sales at 1.9:1. 8 of 11 US sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech and Industrials. Health Care and Staples were the most net bought, an incrementally defensive posture.

All Info Tech subsectors were net sold, led by Software, then Semis & Semi Equipment, then IT Services. In Asia, Korea and Taiwan were the most net sold markets, and foreign investors sold significantly in both overnight on Oct 15.

tension_points.bull_case: Trading sees pockets of overreaction. Neoclouds are down 20% in five sessions, AI exposure is materially reduced, discretionary nets are low and rates are rallying. Demand for compute remains strong and the structural thesis can stay intact, favouring firms with powered capacity and strong balance sheets.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit markets may not be able to finance the AI buildout at the pace planned. Credit is widening across the AI vertical, there are legitimate financing constraints, and the investment cycle could disappoint. Leveraged middlemen such as neoclouds are most exposed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rates stabilizing lower would help the bull case. The report names no specific level that breaks it.

theme_stances.key_argument: Credit widening is a warning on financing the AI buildout, but positioning, valuations and rates are moving in a more supportive direction and the market has overreacted in pockets.
theme_stances.evidence: We should respect what credit is telling us
